chunks.t: As a club officer, you play a specific role in ensuring your club’s success. And by understanding the full scope of your position and how you work with other club officers, your club can thrive by building a culture of collaboration. The importance of serving as a club officer Serving as a club officer gives you the opportunity to set the tone for your club and its members. From encouraging leadership development and training opportunities to keeping your Lion Portal reporting current, onboarding incoming officers and cultivating a sense of belonging, club officers play a key role in the success of the club. For more detailed information about serving as an officer, check out the Club Officer Guide.

View guide Club president/vice president The club president and vice president oversees club operations, presides over board meetings and leads the Global Action Team. Their responsibilities include appointing qualified leadership, adhering to constitutional and legal requirements, guiding and supporting members, and collaborating with district teams on various initiatives. Resource Standard Club Constitution and By-Laws Club secretary The club secretary acts as the link between the club, district and Lions International, supporting smooth operations and member engagement. Responsibilities can include maintaining accurate records, such as meeting minutes, attendance and financial documents, and assisting in creating the club calendar.

Resource Lions Clubs International Shop online store Club treasurer The club treasurer handles the club’s finances by collecting and depositing funds, working with the secretary to send member dues statements, and reporting payments to the board. They pay bills as approved, keep track of all financial records, and share monthly and semi-annual financial updates with the board. A strong membership is vital to the success of your club, district and the Lions Clubs International organization worldwide. Without dedicated members, there would be no one to serve those in need. Lions International offers opportunities for all members to receive recognition for the role they play in growing our organization around the world. Lions International also offers a variety of awards for Lions and Leos involved in the Leo Club Program. For more information on Leo awards, visit the Leo Awards and Recognitions webpage. Awards for Individuals The following awards are opportunities for all Lions to earn, regardless of title:Chevron Award Program This program recognizes Lions for their long-term service, beginning at 10 years, and continuing in 5-year increments.

There are two different types of chevrons, varying slightly in appearance. The Charter Monarch Chevron, available to founding club members only, and the Monarch Chevron. Learn more Membership Key Awards Program This progressive awards program recognizes Lions who sponsor new members that remain active for at least a year. It begins with only two members sponsored, and is something that all Lions can do beginning on their first day of membership. Learn more International Extension Awards The extension awards are presented to two Lions, who, in the opinion of the serving district governor, provided the greatest assistance in the organization of a new Lions club that remains active and in good standing for at least a year.

This is a progressive awards program beginning at just one club, Lions can earn personalized pins for clubs 1-5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 75, 100 and 150 clubs. Learn more Campus Award Pin This pin can be presented to up to two Lions who help charter a Campus Lions club, as determined by the district governor. Learn more Club Branch Pin This prestigious pin is awarded to the first branch liaison when a club branch is formed. Learn more Awards for Clubs The following awards represent some of the ways your club can be recognized for outstanding work in membership development:New Club Sponsor Club Banner Patch Clubs that sponsor a new club receive a banner patch that can proudly be displayed on the club banner.

Learn more Campus Banner Patch Clubs that sponsor a campus club receives a distinctive patch that can be displayed on the club banner. Learn more Club Branch Patch Clubs that serve as a parent to a club branch receive a patch to be displayed on their banner for recognition of their efforts to develop membership. Learn more Membership Satisfaction Award Clubs can earn this prestigious patch that can be displayed on their banner so that all who see it, know that there are happy members. The patch is earned by either retaining 90% of your members for a fiscal year, or by reversing membership losses. Earn additional “tabs” for each subsequent year to affix to your banner for increased recognition.

Learn more Awards for Districts The following awards are earned at the district level by meeting membership development goals:District Governor Extension Award This special pin is awarded to the immediate past district governor who chartered at least one club in during their year as governor, provided the club remains in good standing for at least a year. The pin is personalized to display the number of clubs chartered during their year. Learn more Jesse Robinson Membership Growth Cup The top district team with the largest net percentage of membership growth in each constitutional area will earn the honor of being forever memorialized on the inaugural Jesse Robinson Membership Growth Cup. Each constitutional area will have its own cup.

Each member of the district team (district governor, immediate past district governor, first vice district governor, second vice district governor) will have their names engraved on their constitutional area’s Jesse Robinson Cup, which will honor their incredible achievements for the year. Each member of the district team will also receive a replica cup to recognize their outstanding achievements. Learn more If you have questions or would like more information, please contact us at .

Usable Glasses Give New Life Refractive errors can be easily corrected with eyeglasses, yet millions living in low and middle income countries lack access to basic eye care services. Lions have recognized the urgent need for corrective lenses and collect usable glasses in their communities to support the Lions Recycle For Sight Program. Get Started Today Set up Collection Locations with Local Partners: Invite community partners such as local businesses, schools, optical shops, libraries, places of worship, city administrative centers and eye care professionals to host eyeglass collection boxes. Maintain contact with these partners and schedule regular pick-ups.

Collection Resources: Club Guide for Collecting Used Eyeglasses (iad401) Program brochure, Lions Recycle For Sight (iad403) LCI Eyeglass Collection Box (G1174DS) – order from the Lions Clubs International Shop Promote Your Club's Efforts: The Marketing Communications Chairperson Guide provides tips to help you promote your collection activities and encourage increased community participation. Recognize outstanding collections efforts with a Certificate of Appreciation (iad405) Don't forget to report your service Connect with a Lions Eyeglass Recycling Center (LERC): Send your collected eyeglasses to an official Lions Eyeglass Recycling Center (LERC) for processing. There, the glasses are sorted to determine those that are usable or unusable, processed, and placed in inventory for distribution to optical missions around the world.

Lions help to minimize landfill waste by supporting precious metal reclamation and scrap processing for damaged glasses that are unusable. Lions Eyeglass Recycling Center (LERC) Guidelines: If you are participating in used eyeglass collection, processing and/or distribution activities at a Lions Eyeglass Recycling Center (LERC), or if your district and/or multiple district is considering the establishment of a new LERC, please refer to the Lions Eyeglass Recycling Center (LERC) Guidelines (LERC 425). They oversee the Global Action Team, guide district goals and promote leadership and skills training. In addition to making sure that clubs follow association guidelines and remain in good standing, they also lead key meetings and conventions, foster teamwork across the district and provide service and support to Lions Clubs International Foundation (LCIF) initiatives. Environment Chairpersons serve at the district and multiple district levels, and are appointed by the district governor or council chairperson, respectively. Environment Chairpersons support Lions and Leos engaged or interested in projects to meet environmental challenges at the local and global level. They may collaborate with leadership throughout the organization, including the Global Service Team (GST). Learn Become the topic expert for your district/multiple district by learning about environmental challenges and opportunities. Explore the Sustainable Development Goals, several of which challenge the world to address the issues affecting our environment by 2030. Explore your local environment and consider what service opportunities exist for Lions engagement.

Think about how these opportunities are connected to global environmental challenges and solutions. Explore Lion Portal, LCI/LCIF’s social media sites and the annual Leo Video Contest to learn more about how Lions and Leos are addressing environmental issues in their communities. Discover Bring your knowledge to the local level by exploring how environmental challenges are directly impacting your district/multiple district. Conduct a Community Needs Assessment with a special focus on environment. Contact your local environmental protection agency, or similar organization, to learn about the needs in your area. Identify organizations, including Lions and Leos Clubs in your district/multiple district, which are already mobilized and assess where there are gaps in the services provided.

Plan Based upon what you have learned and discovered, submit a plan of action including recommended service goals for protecting the environment to the district governor/council chairperson for approval. In this process, you may wish to:Meet with organizations already working on environmental issues to discuss how you might support, expand upon or complement their ongoing work. Collaborate with the Youth Camp and Exchange chairperson to organize a Youth Camp that focuses on appreciation and protection of the environment. Discuss your service plan with the GST Coordinator and other leaders, including other programmatic chairpersons, for their feedback. It is possible they are already implementing a project that would benefit from inclusion of an environment-related service element.

Act Inspiring Lion and Leo clubs in your district/multiple district to serve and report their service in Lion Portal will be critical to the success of your plan. Guide clubs in your district/multiple district through the “Learn, Discover, Act” journey as it pertains to the environment. Environment Project Idea List Build awareness of the need, the goals and the service plan by offering an environment-focused seminar and hands-on service activity during district/multiple district convention. Promote funding opportunities offered through LCIF that might support club/district environment projects. Formalize partnerships with other organizations to enhance local impact. Organize a district/multiple district donation to LCIF for disaster relief to increase global impact.

Establish and maintain open communication with the district governor, council chairperson and Global Service Team (GST) leaders. Celebrate Encourage clubs to thoroughly report their environment projects using Lion Portal. Keep the district governor/council chairperson and GST Coordinator informed. Discuss and evaluate progress of the action plan and goals. Share news about environment projects with the Public Relations Chairperson. Celebrate progress and success by recognizing all participating clubs. Contact Us Lions Clubs International Phone: 630-571-5466

Inviting family members to serve with your club is a fantastic way to strengthen and enrich your club’s membership and make being a Lion even more appealing to young adults. Why make your club family-friendly? Adding younger Lions brings new ideas and perspectives that can energize your club. Their children will grow into the next generation of Lion leaders as they develop their skills and a passion. And best of all, more Lions means more service. To encourage families to join and serve together, we offer a 50% discount on international dues for up to four family members who live in the same household and join the same club as a full-paying member. Family Membership is a wonderful way for families to spend quality time together while serving their community.

Family Membership Resources Find out how you can make your club more family-friendly using the resources below. Learn best practices for incorporating younger volunteers into your projects, get tips for accommodating families’ busy schedules and more. Family Membership Brochure Quick-Start Guide Recruitment Poster (Coming Soon) Power Point Presentation The Cub Program Another great way to get families involved is through the Cub Program. This program gives kids 12 and younger a chance to volunteer alongside Lions so they can develop their own lifelong love of service. Cubs don’t need to be related to a Lions member — they just need an interest in serving! The Cub Program can help you build a family-friendly club and bring new energy by getting Cubs involved in club meetings, activities and service projects.
Learn more about the Cub Program and how it can benefit kids and your club.

By sharing our impact through service reporting, Lions and Leos inform, inspire and grow our legacy of humanitarian service. Our global service impact Our service changes lives. In the past fiscal year, Lions and Leos around the world, with support from LCIF, improved the lives of 410 million people. See how we served across our global causes. Childhood Cancer8 million Diabetes14 million Disaster Relief6 million Environment63 million Humanitarian113 million Hunger58 million Vision22 million Youth21 million Benefits for your club Reporting our service helps us highlight our global achievements.

But it also provides even more value for your club, including: Celebrating the impact your club is making Inspiring potential new members to add to your impact Providing leaders with insight on outcomes to better guide your service And that’s not all. Clubs that report service become eligible for awards and recognition, including the Kindness Matters Service Award and the Excellence Awards. See the other ways reporting service benefits your club in the Why Report Service resource. How and when to report service We recommend reporting a service activity in the Lion Portal as soon as possible after you complete your service. The Lion Year ends on June 30, but reports can continue to be entered for that year until July 31.

You can collect the data needed to report an activity with the Service Activity Information resource, which includes a list of our global causes and project types. Training resources and additional information about the Lion Portal can be found on the Lion Portal Updates webpage. Who can report service It’s important for your club to know who is responsible for service reporting, so your club receives the benefits. In Lions clubs, service chairpersons are responsible for service reporting, although many clubs choose to have the club secretary or club president report. In Leo clubs, the president, secretary or Leo club advisor can report service. Your club can also appoint an administrator to handle service reporting or your district can appoint an IT chairperson.

To see all the titles with reporting access, check out the Who Can Report Service resource. How to measure service Our reputation as a leader in global humanitarian service depends on accurate reporting by our clubs. Often, measuring our service impact is straightforward. For example, if your club hosts a diabetes educational event, count the number of people who attend and the volunteers who helped, then report them. In some cases, clubs serve in ways that are more challenging to measure, like cleaning a park, holding a fundraising dinner or promoting awareness of a cause. Learn more about what types of activities can be reported, what metrics are collected and how beneficiaries are counted in the Measuring Service Impact resource.

How districts can help clubs report service Did you know that all districts have a goal to increase the percentage of their clubs that report service? District leaders can access the Insights reports in the Lion Portal to display the number of service activities reported by each club. If you’re a district leader, the following ideas can help your district achieve its reporting goal:Reach out to club leaders. Ask who is responsible for service reporting and how you can help. Share the benefits of service reporting. Encourage clubs to elect a service chairperson, who can assume responsibility for reporting service, if that works for the club. Coach service chairpersons and club secretaries in how to report service by walking them through the steps. Appoint a district IT chairperson who can directly assist clubs with service activity entry.

Why report service Leo-Lion "Service reporting shows what we really do as Leos and Lions. Service data persuades donors and partners. It also gives our members a boost to see the value we provide and everything we do." Kjell Olav Skretting Norway Past District Governor "Service reporting creates transparency. The data from reporting helps generate donations because donors can see how their gifts are used to benefit others." Geraldine Ray USA Past District Governor "Service reporting provides insights into club activities. The information collected helps us promote Lions International and our clubs." Sol Wilfredo Flores Jr. Philippines If you have questions about service reporting, you can find helpful information by visiting our Lions Support webpage. If you can’t find what you’re looking for, email us using the button below.

chunks.h: How to Plan a District Convention
chunks.t: Planning a successful district convention requires you to consider these components: people, planning, preparation and program, and promote. Below, you’ll find the process outlined with helpful resources to assist your team in hosting an amazing convention for the Lions in your district. Getting started Work with the convention team, which handles the district business required to be completed at convention. This includes resolutions, reports and elections, as well as recognizing the accomplishments of the Lions and clubs in the district. How to Plan a District Convention Webinar – Planning a successful district convention requires you to consider these components: People, Planning, Preparation & Program and Promoting. This webinar reviews the available resources, tools and more.

chunks.h: How to Plan a District Convention
chunks.t: The documents and sample forms provided below are in a format which you can easily adjust to meet your district’s specific needs. Many of these tools came from districts whose conventions are successfully held each year. People These are the suggested people you’ll want to take the lead on specific tasks for your convention. Read through their responsibilities and corresponding resources, but keep in mind one person may fill more than one position. District governor: Presiding officer of the business meeting, provides recognition to district Lions and hosts guest speakers and presenters. Convention chairperson: Serves as the governor’s operations officer for the convention. Host committee chairperson: Leads and manages the volunteer Lions eager to welcome the guests to their event.

chunks.h: How to Plan a District Convention
chunks.t: Program chairperson: Responsible for all aspects of the convention program. Finance chairperson: Oversees the finances for the convention. Marketing chairperson: Responsible for the promotion of the convention and events. Audio visual coordinator: Leads the organization of A/V requests for each session and banquets. Planning Planning consists of two steps, outlined below. Gather your questionnaires: These questionnaires are designed for attendees who did come and did not come to the convention. District Convention Attendee Questionnaire Non-Attendee Questionnaire Brainstorm: Use the resources below to gather information that will help you stay on track for a successful event. This includes feedback from both attendees and non-attendees of previous conventions.

chunks.h: How to Plan a District Convention
chunks.t: The responses and insights provided by Lions in your district may provide your team an opportunity to brainstorm on new ideas for the convention program and logistics. Convention Team Brainstorming Questionnaire Results Brainstorming Preparation and program Once your team is formed and ready to go, and your district Lions have let you know what they are seeking to gain in attending your convention, it’s time to start prepping for the event. Your business and production teams will need a master plan that includes a timeline to keep priorities in place including a budget, as well as a task list to assist each chairperson and coordinator in managing their accountabilities. Work closely with the convention team to create a program that meets the needs of the Lions in your district.

Through the International Peace Contests, children around the world have the opportunity to share their feelings and thoughts about peace centered around the year’s theme. Get to know the Peace Contests The International Peace Contests are made up of two unique contests sponsored by Lions clubs — the International Peace Poster Contest and the International Peace Essay Contest. Young people ages 11-13 can share their creativity in expressing what peace means through art and writing. Grand prize winners for each contest receive an award, a monetary prize of US$5,000 and an invitation to a Lions International event. For the International Peace Poster Contest, 23 merit winners will receive a certificate and a monetary prize of US$500.2026-2027 theme: Harmony in Humanity When we treat each other with respect and kindness, peace can flourish.

This year, we invite young people to imagine a world where people of every culture and background live together peacefully — celebrating differences, finding common ground and creating true harmony in humanity. How to participate While both contests are designed for young people (ages 11–13), there are slight differences in criteria. Any young person within the age requirements can participate in a Peace Poster Contest sponsored by a Lions club that has ordered a Peace Poster kit, while the International Peace Essay Contest was specially created for participation by young people with visual impairments. Peace Poster Contest Lions clubs can buy Peace Poster kits from January 15 through October 1. Clubs must send winning posters to the district governor by November 15. Learn more Peace Essay Contest Essay contest rules can be found online.

Clubs must send a winning essay to the district governor on November 15. Learn more Meet the winners Be inspired by the creativity of the current and past winners of the International Peace Contests. #Peace Poster on Social

The First Vice District Governor/District Governor-Elect (FVDG/DGE) Training Program is a year-long initiative that prepares FVDGs/DGEs with essential knowledge and leadership skills to support their districts and Lions International. The training program includes self-paced online assignments, a live virtual seminar, an in-person seminar at the international convention, and a vice district governor multiple district/single district workshop (VDG MD/SD) organized locally by multiple/single district Global Leadership Team (GLT) coordinators or Global Action Team (GAT) area leaders. Please see the FVDG/DGE Program Overview for a view of the entire FVDG/DGE Training Program. Below you will find detailed information pertaining to the FVDG/DGE Training Program and the international convention.

FVDG/DGE Virtual SeminarDGE Seminar at Convention Online and local learning Resources FVDG/DGE Virtual Seminar Who: FVDG/DGEWhen: February/March 2027The FVDG/DGE Virtual Seminar is an interactive virtual learning experience designed for FVDGs/DGEs to connect with their peers, share insights and strengthen their leadership skills. This virtual seminar features inspiring presentations from the international first vice president, pre-assignments, and live virtual training sessions led by a group leader certified through the Lions Certified Instructor Program.

DGE Seminar at Convention Who: DGE and spouse or adult companion Seminar: Wednesday, June 30 – Friday, July 2, 2027Arrival: Tuesday, June 29, 2027Departure: Wednesday, July 7, 2027DGEs and their spouse or adult companion will experience engaging discussions, interactive learning and inspiring presentations. Highlights include a photo opportunity with the incoming international president, motivational guest speakers, engaging activities and a special presentation tailored for DGEs' spouse/adult companion. The seminar concludes with the highly anticipated DGE Celebration Banquet. Register now Schedule - coming soon Know Before You Go Checklist - coming soon Onsite Experience - coming soon Travel visaDGEs and their spouse/adult companion may need a visa to travel to the DGE Seminar at Convention.

If a travel visa is required, we recommend beginning the visa application process as soon as possible. For more information visit the convention webpage. Travel reimbursement First Vice District Governors/District Governors-Elect traveling to convention for seminar training must submit their expense claims through the Lion Portal. Paper submissions will not be accepted. Online and local learning Along with the in-person and virtual seminar, there are online and local learning opportunities included in the training program. FVDGs/DGEs are assigned a collection of e Learning courses via their custom learning path, and will participate in a joint workshop with the second vice district governors (SVDGs) in their area. Review the following to learn more.

Online assignmentsFVDGs/DGEs will be assigned online courses to complete throughout their year of training. The courses will be automatically assigned as they become available in the Lions Learning Center (LLC), which can be accessed through the Lion Portal. For further support, email  or view Lions Learning Center (LLC) access instructions. Lions Learning CenterVDG Multiple/Single District Workshop Lions International provides resources and curriculum for multiple districts and single districts to conduct a joint workshop for SVDGs and FVDGs in their area. The instructor-led workshop is organized by multiple/single district GLT coordinators in consultation with the GAT area leaders. Visit the Leadership Development Multiple District Grant Program webpage for more information.

celebrate Lions at all levels The Excellence Awards honor clubs and Lion leaders who demonstrate outstanding leadership, membership growth, impactful service and humanitarian contributions.2026-2027 updates | Club criteria | Zone, region and district criteria | Road to excellence 2026-2027 Excellence Awards updates These prestigious awards are available at four levels—club, zone, region and district. Clubs must earn a Club Excellence Award as a prerequisite for Excellence Awards at the zone, region and district level. Applications will not be necessary for the 2026-2027 award cycle. Awards will be distributed by Lions International to clubs that meet the updated criteria and eligibility requirements. You will find these listed below. *New clubs chartered after January 1, 2027, are not eligible for the award.

Club Excellence Award criteria The Club Excellence Award acknowledges the dedication and legacy of service within individual clubs and is the foundation for excellence awards presented to zone chairpersons, region chairpersons and district governors. Membership Achieved a net growth of two (2) members or 10% or more members, whichever is greater. (Reinstated members and charter members above the minimum 20 members will qualify.) Or sponsor a new Lions club or club branch. Service Report a minimum of four (4) service activities. Three (3) must align with our Global Causes around Youth, Vision and Environment (one in each Global Cause); these service projects can be completed throughout the 2026-2027 Lion year. Leadership Clubs in Good Standing: not in Status Quo or Financial Suspension.

Club dues paid and no unpaid balance with Lions International greater than US$50 outstanding 90 days or more. Report newly elected club officers for the 2027-2028 Lion year in the Lion Portal by May 15, 2027 of the current Lion year. Club officers (President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer) to attend instructor-led club officer training (in person or virtual), organized and reported in Learn by GLT coordinator, or online through the Lions Learning Center between March 1, 2026 – October 31, 2026. The club president for the current Lion year must not have served more than two consecutive terms. A minimum of 10% of the club’s members complete any three (3) courses in the Lions Learning Center. Donations Contributed to LCIF a minimum of the club’s membership total at the start of the 2026-2027 Lion year multiplied by US$20.

Zone, region and district criteria Earning the Club Excellence Award is key to becoming eligible for the Zone, Region and District Excellence Awards. These awards will be distributed based on meeting criteria for each category. Zone Excellence Award The Zone Excellence Award recognizes outstanding Zone Chairpersons who cultivate growth and excellence within their clubs. To qualify, 50% of the clubs within the zone must earn the Club Excellence Award. Region Excellence Award The Region Excellence Award honors exceptional Region Chairpersons and regional success. To qualify, 50% or more of the clubs within the region must earn the Club Excellence Award, highlighting commitment to fostering high-performing, service-driven clubs.

District Excellence Award The District Excellence Award recognizes District Governors who drive exceptional growth, leadership and community impact. To qualify, 50% or more of the clubs within the district must earn the Club Excellence Award, demonstrating commitment to Lions International core principles. The road to excellence Increase your chances of earning an award by increasing your level of service through engagement in activities that promote Lions excellence. Participate in the Global Causes Amplify your club’s impact by participating in the Service Journey. It is an approach to making a difference people can see and feel. Learn more about the global causes and what your club can do to support Youth, Vision and Environment.

Invite new friends New members are critical to the club’s success, so spread the word about why you love being a Lion. Whether it’s the community, sense of belonging or joy of helping others, serving as a Lion is always more fun with a friend. Plus, every time you invite a new member, you are helping us reach our MISSION 1.5 goals so that we can serve even more people!Empower service around the world With 100% of donations going towards grants and programs, your generosity to LCIF allows us to serve people in need. Please consider donating to the Lions Clubs International Foundation today and thank you for your support! Contact us For questions or inquiries email us at .

Getting started with supporting Leos Lead the next generation Leo Club Advisors Leo club advisors As a Leo club advisor, your enthusiasm about working with young people and guiding Leos in club management and service is key to ensuring their success. In addition, you play an important role in kickstarting the collaboration between Leos and your Lions club, creating an environment for learning and connecting Leos with other community leaders. Understanding your role Some responsibilities of your role can vary depending on your Leos’ ages — Omega Leos may require different support than Alpha Leos, like when executing service projects or developing leadership skills. But regardless of which club you’re sponsoring, there are tasks that you’ll need to support and training to help you do it.

Talk to Lion leaders supporting Leos Be sure to maintain open communication with the district and multiple district Leo chairpersons, as well as Leo leaders at those levels, to ensure full support for your Leo club. Report your Leos Take time to report any new Leo members, clubs and service projects in the Lion Portal to help track the health of the club and to see the service impact Leos have made. Learn more about the importance of reporting in the Reporting Matters Guide. Order supplies Explore Leo-branded items in the Lions Shop to help recognize your Leos and show your Leo pride. You can also order recruitment materials and the Leo Club Program Handbook using the Leo Club Publications Order Form.

Attend a Leo forum Leo forums can help you understand the Leo Club Program and network with other Lions and Leos so you can find new ideas for service, build connections and more. You can also find more information about what your role entails in the Leo Club Program Handbook. Supporting Leos’ next service steps As Leos consider serving as a Lion or approach the end of their time in the Leo Club Program, it’s important to talk with them about continuing their service journey and to let them know they have options. Alpha Leos may find Omega Leos to be a natural next step. In addition to Omega Leos, encouraging Leos to become Lions is an excellent way to help Leos to continue to grow their impact.

If Alpha or Omega Leos do not transfer their membership before aging out of the Leo Club Program, their respective records will be automatically closed, or end-dated, by Lions International annually on June 30 according to Board Policy Chapter XXII, Article V., C. Be sure to let your Leos know that continuing their service journey will help keep their service record intact. Other ways to help your Leos In addition to the logistical steps required in your role, there are other steps you can take to help your Leos and your Leo club grow. Set your club up for success Learn how you and your fellow Lions club officers can help your Leo club start strong with tips on member recruitment, promoting the club and much more.

Learn more Help your Leos thrive See all the other ways you can help your Leos find success by mentoring your Leos, encouraging the use of the Leo Advancement Sessions and more. Explore available awards, grants and training opportunities available. Learn more Trainings The Leo Club Advisor Training is designed to give you a clearer understanding of both the Leo Club Program and your role as an advisor. The training includes six modules that cover important tips, tools and resources that can help you find success in supporting your Leos. Module 1: Leo Club Program overview Learn about the history, purpose and structure of the Leo Club Program.

Power Point Module 2: The role of the Leo club advisor Get a better understanding of the responsibilities of your role as well as strategies for serving as effective advisors and promoting positive youth development. Power Point Module 3: Leo club administration Review the key administrative functions of Leo clubs including fees, bank accounts, elections, reporting, meetings and important dates. Power Point Module 4: Leo Club Program resources from Lions International Learn about resources and tools available from Lions International to support Leo club advisors. Power Point Module 5: Working with younger people Find tips for how to successfully work with young people. Power Point Module 6: Continuing the Leo to Lion service journey Learn about the different Lions membership paths Leos can take after their service in the Leo Club Program.

Through a Leo-Lion club, you can create new opportunities to continue your service and provide a supportive environment for Young Lions to grow. The benefit of Leo-Lion clubs Chartering a Leo-Lion club opens up a world of opportunities to grow your impact as a Young Lion, Leo-Lion or Leo looking to continue your service, including:Broadening your visibility and reach within your community Expanding your service impact with service activities that meet your interests Providing a welcoming space for Young Lions and a diverse array of people within your community How to charter a club When chartering a new Leo-Lion club, there are a few considerations to keep in mind that differ from starting a standard Lions club.

Charter member requirements New Leo-Lion clubs require a minimum of 20 charter members, 10 of which must be former Leo members who have served for at least one year and one day as a Leo. Once the club is established, there is no requirement to have 10 former Leos at any given time. Involving additional younger members Keep in mind other members who may benefit from joining or chartering a Leo-Lion club. Young Adult membership is an exclusive membership type for those ages 30 and younger who join or charter a Leo-Lion club. There is no requirement to be a former Leo to serve as a Young Adult member, and these members can receive a 50% discount on international dues and a charter or entrance fee waiver when they join a Leo-Lion club.

Reporting in Lion Portal Your former Leo members should be transferred to the Leo-Lion club within the Lion Portal rather than added as new members in order to have their Leo and Lion record merged. Then, once you have your required 20-plus members, you must declare your club type as “Leo-Lion.”Special considerations Additional approval from the Membership Development Committee is required when a district charters over 3 new Leo-Lion clubs or adds over 100 Leo-Lion or Young Adult charter members seeking discounted dues in a fiscal year. Learn more about this in Chapter X of Board Policy. Expectations for your new club Once you’ve chartered your Leo-Lion club, it’s important to maintain the momentum and the excitement shared by your new members.

Be sure to set expectations with your charter members, but keep the following in mind for long-term success. Connect to your Lion community by participating in local, district, multiple district and international events Recruit new Lions through service Ensure meetings are efficient and engaging Take the next step If you’re ready to charter a new Leo-Lion club, connect with your district leadership, then visit the Start a New Club webpage to find additional information about the next steps. Network and grow your new club Be sure to connect with your community of Lions, Leo-Lions and Leos to ensure your club’s success — and membership growth — once you’ve chartered your Leo-Lion club. If you’re already a Leo-Lion, make the most of your time and encourage Leos to join your club as new Leo-Lions.
If you’re a current Leo, see what your next step could look like — and how Leo-Lion membership could be just what you’re looking for.

Rebuilding and reactivating struggling and cancelled clubs helps grow not only the impact in our communities, but also helps boost our membership — giving us more hands for more service. Club Rebuilding Use the following steps to assist struggling clubs: Step 1:Review the Club Health Assessment for club status (status quo and cancelled clubs), membership loss and account balance over 90 days. Clubs should make sure the roster is up to date and drop members who have left the club so they do not incur additional expenses. Step 2:Determine strategy If the club is small but in good standing, consider Club Rebuilding. Enlist the support of a Guiding Lion or encourage the zone chairperson to mentor the club in recruiting new members, training officers and providing meaningful community service.

For clubs needing assistance, please fill out the Club Rebuilding Application and obtain the appropriate signatures. If the club is in status quo, the district should work with the club to bring them to good standing. See the Club Health Assessment for the reason the club was placed on status quo. When ready fill out the Club Reactivation Form. For clubs in status quo for Financial Suspension to be returned to Good Standing, their outstanding balance must be paid. This can be found in the Lion Portal or by contacting the A/R & Club Account Services Department at . If the club has been cancelled:Disbanded: Districts have 12 months from the date of cancellation to reactive the club. A minimum of 10 members is required and any outstanding balance with Lions International must be paid. See the Club Reactivation Form for more information.

Financial Suspension: For clubs to be returned to Good Standing, their outstanding balance must be paid. This can be found the Lion Portal or by contacting the A/R and Club Account Services Department at . If reactivated, the club must pay the balance in full along with approval form the district governor. See the Financial Suspension Reactivation Form for this purpose. The Club Rebuilding Learning Path is an online tool available to all Lions clubs, currently offered in English only. This resource provides eight courses to help clubs grow, thrive and rebuild through teamwork, goal setting, strategic planning and improving overall club health. To accommodate each club’s unique members and goals, the course offers a flexible framework. Contact  to participate.

Step 3:Encourage the zone chairperson and if needed assign a Guiding Lion to assist the club. Guiding Lion Assignment Form. Visit the Guiding Lion webpage for more information. Key resources View the below resources to help a club become successful. Building club leadership Webpages Club President/Vice President Club Secretary Club Treasurer Club Membership Chairperson Club Service Chairperson Club Marketing ChairpersonLCIF Coordinator Guide Club officer guide Membership growth Just Ask! guide Membership application Club membership chairpersons guide Club membership chairperson webpage Club operations Plan for your club’s success guide Plan for your club's success Power Point Your club your way Club quality initiative workbook Training Visit the Lions Learning Center under Learn in the Lion Portal.

Under “course catalog” there are four courses available for club officer training:Club Officer Training Club President Responsibilities Club Secretary Responsibilities Club Treasurer Responsibilities Awards Club Excellence Awards The Club Excellence Award honors clubs and Lion leaders who demonstrate outstanding leadership, membership growth, impactful service and humanitarian contributions. To learn more, visit the Excellence Award webpage. Certified Guiding Lion Award As part of the Club Rebuilding Program, a Guiding Lion is assigned to the club who acts as a mentor. The Guiding Lion assists the areas in which they may need help. Upon the completion of the two-year term, Guiding Lions may qualify for the Guiding Lion Award.

Requirements for the Guiding Lion to qualify for the award are listed below broken out by the club and the Guiding Lion:Club requirements:Is in good standing with Lions International. Had a net membership growth and a minimum of 20 members at the close of the Guiding Lion’s two-year term. Reported new service and fundraising projects and was encouraged to donate to LCIF. Participated in district activities (including zone meetings). Club officers confirm the Guiding Lion supported the club’s development (sign the final report form). Guiding Lion requirements: Submitted Quarterly Reports to Lions International and the district governor for two years. Completed the Certified Guiding Lion Course prior to the end of their two year assignment. Attended a majority of the club’s general and board meetings.

Submitted their Final Report to Lions International and their district governor. Contact us For further information or to inquire about club rebuilding and club reactivation, please contact us at  or phone (630) 468-7084.
